A7_S2_D1: ^Narrator: The world under the surface softly greets your eyes.
^Narrator: The sunlight is gentle, the water is clear, and…
^Narrator: Your hair doesn't float up into your face either, since they're tentacles now.
^Narrator: She’s one of the Ichthyos girls who was stuck under the rock!
^Ada: You’re the one who brought the boat over, right? Really saved our skins there.
choiceada: ^Ada: Good as new! We Ichthyos heal faster when we exercise and eat.
^Narrator: A swarm of other people in the distance catches your eye. Ada smiles.
A7_S2_D2: ^Noelle: (You can really feel how strong the waves are from here!)
^Narrator: Your awe is cut short when Zale grabs onto a fish, and immediately bites down on it to knock it unconscious.
^Narrator: The Ichthyos join him, laughing gleefully as they enjoy their breakfast…
^Hugo: In the same way some predatory creatures may consume meat, so do the Ichthyos.
^Hugo: We Krakenfolk prefer to cook our seafood first, though…
^Hugo: We do have some vegetarians on shore. You can find some bread and soups like they serve in the human settlement once you resurface.
^Narrator: You hear the Krakenfolk in the fishing boats above call out. They’ve stuck their heads into the water to ask the others to start passing them supplies.
^Aditi: We haven’t got all day, y’know!
^Hugo: I’ll go help them. Talk to you soon?
^Narrator: You’re starting to realize that this is the first time you’ve encountered meat.
^Narrator: The humans eat eggs and sometimes fish, you’ve heard… but that’s only when they’re brought over as gifts from the ocean.
^Noelle: (At least they’re only taking what they need, I guess…?)
^Narrator: As the day continues, with the Ichthyos and Krakenfolk guiding you further away from shore…
^Narrator: You begin to realize a few things.
^Noelle: (They can predict the weather and tides for the next week just by sensing it from the water… and monitor how long we have until the floods come in.)
^Noelle: (Not to mention that they’re acquainted with so many sea creatures. Despite their playful sides, the Ichthyos are paying close attention to everything around them.)
^Noelle: Trying to figure out how to swim faster. I can tell you guys are going easy on me.
^Noelle: …To be honest, this is kind of amazing. I never would’ve imagined that I’d be able to come down underwater for so long.
^Ada: If you’re up for it, I can show you how to move faster, ‘see’ your surroundings while you’re swimming.
^Ada: Before you know it, it’s easier than it is to walk!
^Noelle: I probably look like a duckling, don’t I?
^Ada: Oh, it’s nothing. All the Krakenfolk were the same.
^Ada: Some were even afraid of the water!
^Narrator: As the next days pass, you continue joining the Ichthyos and Krakenfolk in their daily activities.
^Narrator: As you return to the usual diving spot, you realize that Ada’s right.
^Narrator: Going underwater now feels as easy as breathing air.
A7_S2_D3: ^Ada: Hey, you! Already used to the ocean I see!
^Noelle: Spending time here has been really nice.
^Noelle: I’m used to busying myself with other things, and never really thought about my new features that much…
^Ada: Ha, your kind tends to be like that, sometimes. You’re like our slightly strange, overachieving cousins!
^Narrator: You think about the way the Ichthyos like to bulldoze into the Krakenfolk and drop their scavenged items into their arms.
^Noelle: I guess it’s a human thing to have too many concerns.
^Noelle: I can tell that you guys have helped out the Krakenfolk a lot.
^Ada: Well… we’re the most energetic of the Thavma. And one could say the most ‘creature-like.’
^Ada: I guess we understand how small one can feel against the big, wide ocean. That’s why we always travel in packs!
^Noelle: (They’re so free-willed that it’s almost healing.)
^Noelle: (Ah… things back home really were strict.)
^Ada: Your homeland isn’t fond of creatures, are they?
^Ada: That must have been hard… I can’t imagine being treated differently just because of how I looked.
^Narrator: Not wanting to bring the mood down, you give Ada a light smile.
^Noelle: Well… if you want to cheer me up, maybe you can show me how you guys do that spinning thing that speeds you up.
^Ada: Oh, you just need to get the hang of it.
^Ada: Zale loves that trick. Let’s find him and go through his favourite track!
^Narrator: The trick is to swim fast enough to ‘move’ the current your way, then create a boost of energy that burrows you through the water at record speed.
^Narrator: …At least, that is the best way to describe it, for one who isn’t experiencing it themself.
^Narrator: Soon, the day wanes, and you finally resurface to find Amelia happily munching on grilled fish, which she’s taken to help grill over their firepits over the last few days.
